stages.breaks: Having no hours when both teams are online.
stages.why: Every question waits a day, and a two-day task becomes a week.
stages.does: We agree an overlap window with you, write it into the scope and keep a daily check-in inside it.

stages.breaks: Letting work stall between time zones.
stages.why: You start the day without knowing what moved or what is blocked.
stages.does: An end-of-day note covering done, blocked and next, sent before your day starts.

stages.breaks: Leaving invoicing and currency for later.
stages.why: Billing friction wastes your finance team's time and delays approvals.
stages.does: Invoice currency and terms are agreed before work starts, so billing is boring, as it should be.

stages.why: Shared passwords and open folders put your client's data and your contract at risk.
stages.does: An NDA and written terms before access, scoped logins and a record of who can see what.

stages.k: Do not depend on one person
stages.breaks: Depending on one person on the partner side.
stages.why: When they are away, the work stops, and you find out from the client.
stages.does: A pod with a second person on every account, and a coordinator who keeps the queue moving.
